title: Adī-Kadi Vav & Navghan Kuvo - Ancient Stepwells of Junagadh
content:
Adī-Kadi Vav & Navghan Kuvo, Junagadh

Nestled within the historic Uparkot Fort in Junagadh, Adī-Kadi Vav and Navghan Kuvo are among the oldest and most fascinating stepwells in Gujarat. These architectural marvels not only reflect ancient water management techniques but also tell stories of faith, sacrifice, and resilience.

Adī-Kadi Vav

Built around the 15th century, Adī-Kadi Vav is an extraordinary stepwell carved directly into solid rock, featuring 120 steps descending deep into the earth. Legend says that two women named Adi and Kadi were sacrificed to make water flow in the well, hence the name. Though the legend remains a mystery, the well continues to fascinate visitors with its spiritual and historical aura.

Navghan Kuvo

Situated nearby, Navghan Kuvo is even older, believed to have been constructed around the 500-700 CE during the reign of the Chudasama dynasty. It was used as a water source for the royal family during times of siege. Unlike Adī-Kadi Vav, this stepwell is circular and cut deep into soft rock, showcasing exceptional craftsmanship and ingenuity in early Indian architecture.

Together, these two stepwells stand as a symbol of Gujarat’s rich heritage and engineering brilliance. The peaceful surroundings and the intricate rock-carved structure make this site a must-visit for history lovers, photographers, and spiritual seekers alike.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Adī-Kadi Vav and Navghan Kuvo is from October to February, when the weather is cool and ideal for sightseeing in Junagadh.

How to Reach

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Rajkot Airport, around 100 km from Junagadh.
  • By Train: Junagadh has its own railway station, well-connected to major cities in Gujarat.
  • By Road: Regular buses and taxis are available from Rajkot, Somnath, and Ahmedabad.

Nearby Places to Visit: 

  • Uparkot Fort: The fort where the stepwells are located, known for its ancient walls and Buddhist caves. Read more..
  • Mahabat Maqbara: A stunning mausoleum known for its Indo-Islamic architecture. Read more..
  • Girnar Hills: A sacred pilgrimage site with ancient temples and scenic trekking routes. Read more..
  • Sakkarbaug Zoological Park: One of India’s oldest zoos, located just a few kilometers away. Read more..
